tasks.question: Within godot/assets/marble_machine/environment/environment_world.gd, every terrain feature this file scatters (crests, boulders, spires, trees, landmarks, anchors) is only placed after passing through one specific function that decides whether a candidate site is valid, checking clearance from both the racing line and the camera path in a single call. Identify: (a) the exact symbol responsible for that combined placement-validity decision, (b) its kind, (c) its exact line span on this checkout, (d) the exact lower-level symbol(s) it calls to measure each of the two clearances, and (e) the smallest surrounding implementation body a change to how placement validity is decided would need to touch. Do not include the sibling function that only explains a rejection in human-readable form without itself deciding validity.
tasks.why_tests_provider_utility: environment_world.gd is 1618 lines with ~28 static functions. A structural symbol index (Ctags or tree-sitter) can answer 'what functions exist and where' in one bounded query, versus Grep needing several pattern guesses (_sited, _clear, _track_gap, _why all match loosely-related search terms) and Read needing to page through a large file. This is the profile Benchmark C2's own design predicted a provider should plausibly help with, and which C2 never actually tested because the provider was never called.

tasks.question: Two mesh cross-section builder functions defined once in godot/scripts/toy_geometry.gd -- beam_section() and channel_section() -- are called from other production scene-building GDScript files (files that construct an actual Node3D/mesh scene, not diagnostic or reporting scripts) to build swept support and channel geometry. Identify every production scene file that calls either function, and for each one: every call site's enclosing symbol and line, and which of the two functions it calls (a file may call one, the other, or both, more than once). Do not include a file merely because it preloads/references toy_geometry.gd for unrelated geometry helpers. Do not include a file whose own locally-defined function happens to share one of these two names without actually calling toy_geometry.gd's version.
tasks.why_tests_provider_utility: 36 files reference toy_geometry.gd overall, but only 3 actually call beam_section/channel_section, under two different local aliases (Geometry, Geo), plus one file (v2_track.gd) that defines its own same-named, differently-shaped local function as a realistic false positive, and one file (toy_geometry_check.gd) that is a genuine caller but out of the 'production scene' scope by design. A reference-aware provider should in principle distinguish real calls from mere co-references and from same-name shadowing faster than serial Grep passes across 36 candidate files.
